source: The Sun warms water so it evaporates into vapor. The vapor rises, cools and condenses into clouds. Water falls as rain or snow (precipitation) and collects in oceans, lakes, rivers and the ground.
Thinking clouds are made of water vapor or cotton-like steam. Clouds are billions of tiny drops of liquid water or bits of ice.
The water in your glass may once have been part of a cloud, a glacier or the ocean. Earth's water goes round and round in the water cycle.
The water cycle. The Sun powers it.

Evaporation: the Sun warms water and it rises as invisible water vapor. Condensation: high up, the vapor cools into tiny drops that make clouds. Precipitation: drops join, grow heavy and fall as rain, snow, sleet or hail. Collection: water gathers in oceans, lakes, rivers and under the ground, and the cycle starts again.
Plants add water vapor to the air too, from tiny holes in their leaves. Most of Earth's water, about 97 out of every 100 drops, is salty ocean water.
When seawater evaporates, the salt stays behind. That is why rain is fresh water even though so much of it came from the salty ocean.
On a cold morning, drops of water form on the outside of a glass of ice water. Which step is that?
The drops came from water vapor in the air.
The cold glass cooled the vapor into liquid drops.
Thinking clouds are made of water vapor or smoke. Clouds are made of tiny drops of liquid water or bits of ice, so small they float.
